en.title: Amazon OA #44: Get Encoded Name (Lexicographically Smallest Palindrome)
en.description: You are given a string letters that contains only lowercase letters and is itself a palindrome. Rearrange its characters and, among all rearrangements that are still palindromes, output the lexicographically smallest one.
en.input: A single line containing the string letters. 1≤|letters|≤3×10^7; it contains only lowercase letters a-z, and letters is a palindrome.
en.output: Output one line: the lexicographically smallest palindromic rearrangement.
en.explanation: Example 1: the characters of yxxy are two x and two y; the palindromic rearrangements are xyyx and yxxy, and the smaller one is xyyx. Example 2: in cbabc, a appears once and can only go in the center; the first half takes b and c, giving bcacb. Example 3: baab is rearranged into abba.
hints: A palindrome is determined by its first half and its center character.
Since the input is a palindrome, at most one letter occurs an odd number of times, and it must go in the center.
Arranging the first half in non-decreasing letter order is enough.
